situations: A big group photo of students in uniform cheering on the school steps.
A group of young men, likely ex-students, pose together at night on a street decorated with festival lights.
A plain selfie photo of a middle-aged man in glasses.
A poster announcing that the 'one-point demand' is loading, i.e. the movement is escalating.
A screenshot of a phone note listing the Bangla exam suggestion (expansion of ideas, essays, paragraphs) is shared before the exam.
A small cropped face photo of a man, probably a teacher, with no joke on it.
A teacher plays chess against a student while classmates crowd around to watch.
Alumni association programme schedule for the school's 150-year celebration on 24-26 December.
Candid photo of an older man (likely a teacher) standing by a railing.
Not a meme. It's a page announcement / notice graphic
Official banner announcing 150th anniversary registration, contacts and attractions.
Official banner announcing the school's 150th anniversary celebration and registration details.
Official logo for the school's 150th anniversary celebration.
Photo of protest graffiti painted on the school's boundary wall.
Plain photo of the painted murals on the school's boundary wall.
Protest graffiti painted on the school's boundary wall during a national political movement.
Registration poster for the school's 150-year anniversary celebration.
Shared local news about an abandoned newborn girl who died after being found under a culvert.
The meme page's own logo: school crest with a lion, flames and a pain meter.
The official school emblem.
The official school logo/seal.
The page posts a Ramadan greeting over a picture of the school gate.
The page posts a Ramadan greeting.
The page posts an Eid-ul-Adha greeting over a rainy photo of the school field and promises new memes.
The page posts an Eid-ul-Adha greeting to its followers.
The page shares a university notice banning iftar parties on campus.
The page shares its follower count milestone.
The page temporarily rebrands itself as 'Bangladesh Pain' in a blood-dripping logo.
The page's Eid greeting post.
The page's logo glowing inside the head of a person with a headache, as page branding.
The page's own logo.
why_relatable: Students recognise their school logo; used as page identity.

situations: A class ten student who has never bunked school is treated like a primitive caveman.
A student bunking school suddenly bumps into a teacher halfway and runs to hide anywhere.
A student bunks school by walking straight out through the main gate and feels like a daredevil.
A student fakes a stomach ache to get leave from school, then becomes perfectly happy the moment he is out of the gate.
A student skips assembly by hiding in a corner under the stairs, but the teacher still finds him.
A student who bunked school feels relaxed at bedtime, then remembers the teacher has their father's phone number.
A student who has tried both going to class and skipping it decides the real fun is in bunking.
A teacher praises a student for never bunking school all year, while the truth is he simply can't climb the wall to escape.
A teacher spots you hanging around outside another school and calls you over, and you and your friend decide not to go because you'll get beaten.
After bunking school one day, the student gets thoroughly beaten the next day.
As soon as a certain song plays, students throw their bags over and climb the school wall to escape.
Friends bunk school together, but once a teacher catches them everyone pretends they don't know each other
School boys sneak out by climbing over the walls and roofs, set to Brahmanbaria Liberation Day text.
Students caught trying to bunk school stand lined up looking guilty in front of the building.
Students in uniform climb over the school boundary wall to escape while one is already down on the road.
Students in uniform climb over the school wall one after another to bunk class.
Students trying to escape school spot a teacher on the other side and scramble to hide or get back in.
Students who skipped morning PT and stayed hiding in the empty classroom panic when a teacher comes in with a cane to check.
Trying to teach your chubby friend how to bunk school (climb the wall and escape).
Uniformed students climb over the school boundary wall to escape during school hours.
Uniformed students throw their bags over the school wall and climb over it to escape school.
When Ramadan comes, ex-students everywhere remember climbing over the school wall to bunk.
why_relatable: Every student has seen 'we're in this together' collapse the moment a teacher starts asking who else was involved

situations: A group post asking about students' favourite teacher stays pending forever, never approved.
A join requester names another school's headmistress and says they have no favourite Annada teacher.
A member's join-request answer calls the headmistress 'respected Farida madam' with exaggerated politeness, and the admin shares it.
A member's join-request answers for the school's Facebook group give the headmistress's name mixed up with a famous politician's name, and the admin shares the screenshot.
A requester to the boys' school group names a different school's headmistress, exposing they are not from the school.
A teacher is tagged on a meme post but Facebook says he can't see it because he isn't in the group.
Alumni warn students not to disrespect teachers, and the meme page that constantly roasts teachers awkwardly looks away.
Imagining what a strict teacher would do if he caught the meme page admin red-handed.
In the comments, friends tease each other about being 'bitten by the pink snake' (heartbroken by a girl), and the page admin asks one to inbox the page.
News of defamation and cyberbullying cases against meme pages makes the school meme page nervously look away.
One teacher suggests cutting 10 marks from everyone in the students' meme group and another agrees.
Someone asking to join the school group answers the batch question with 'yes' but names the headmaster correctly.
Someone from a different school requests to join the school group and still answers the screening question with our headmaster's name.
Someone requests to join the group but ignores the membership questions, leaving the admin to decide.
The meme page jokes that after posting edgy political memes it 'lost' a huge investment offer.
The meme page's inbox is full of students offering school gossip and inside info in exchange for favours.
The page's English name 'Annada Pain' is rejected and a literal Bangla translation 'Annada Byatha' is preferred.
Yet another requester names a different school's headmistress while trying to join the school group.
why_relatable: Group admins see silly answers to screening questions every day, and 'yes' is the classic careless reply.

situations: A character advises that you can't survive in this world unless you are a bit subtle.
A guy takes a selfie video in front of a huge crowd of ex-students gathered on the school steps.
A man in sunglasses and blazer dances happily in a crowded bus.
A neglected corner of the school wall is shown with maths formulas floating over it.
A photo of a middle-aged man in a panjabi posing with a smiling young woman in festive pink clothes. There is no text, so the joke must be in the caption.
A student has to choose between two teachers (e.g. whose class or private batch to follow).
A student reacting with overwhelming emotion to something (exact situation likely in post caption).
A veiny-armed driver at a Toyota steering wheel heads straight toward the Twin Towers.
An elderly bearded man gives a speech into a microphone at a 2005 batch celebration event.
Fan girls of a certain group pretend not to see something embarrassing about their idols.
News footage of the army deployed on the streets during a period of unrest, posted without visible school framing.
School life gets progressively more chaotic from class 6 to class 8, shown as a man being woken up again and again at night.
Screenshot of a named person's Facebook post telling students to trust the Prime Minister during the protests, shared to call him out.
Screenshot of an old Annada Pain video post showing two people fighting or dancing on a courtyard.
The saying 'a teacher ranks right after a father' is paired with a photo of a political figure flashing a V-sign as 'the teacher'.
Three grown men laugh together over cups of tea on a bench at a roadside tea stall.
UNCLEAR: there's no school angle visible in the video itself
why_relatable: Students lived through the shutdown/unrest period together; the school angle is probably in the post caption.
characters: three adult men (possibly teachers or alumni)

situations: A famous footballer is edited in front of the school gate bragging that Annada students are the best in Brahmanbaria.
A student brags that his school is the best in town, and an outsider asks if the teachers actually teach well in class, and he goes silent.
An Annada student swaggers through the city causing chaos, then acts surprised that people can tell which school he is from.
Asked about results, science fairs, debates and sports, the school's students respond with total indifference or an absurd answer.
Asked about results, science fairs, debates or sports, students of the school confidently boast that their school is world-class at everything.
Every student at the school secretly dreams of getting out of it.
Every student's real dream is simply to get out of the school.
Searching 'Pain' on a map gives directions straight to the school.
Searching for 'Pain' on a map takes you straight to your own school.
Students brag that their school is the best, but the obvious follow-up 'teachers teach well in class, right?' gets awkward silence
Students proudly declare that their school is the best in the town.
The school building with caged, grilled windows and scribbled walls looks more like a jail than a proud old school.
The school is great at hype, talent, science fairs and debates, weak at actual studying, and its BNCC is below zero.
The school's founder is shown taking a victory walk in front of a huge crowd after creating the best school in the district.
While studying in another district, you unexpectedly meet someone from your old school and greet them like a long-lost brother.
why_relatable: Famous schools' students know the reputation is real but classroom teaching isn't; everyone relies on coaching/private tuition
specificity: only your school (format works for any 'best school')

card: Rivalry / comparison with neighbouring girls' schools
situations: A news-style reporter standing in front of the neighbouring girls' school gate describes it as 'a modern poultry farm'.
A student claims girls of one girls' school are prettier than the other and is shouted down.
Boys argue about which neighbouring girls' school is better, and anyone who disagrees gets kicked from the group chat
Facebook keeps recommending the neighbouring girls' school page to the boys' school meme page, which treats it as endless meme material.
Facebook suggests pages similar to the neighbouring girls' school, exposing whose page you have been checking.
In a 'ghosts from different countries' list, Bangladesh's ghost 'Shakchunni' is shown as a photo of the neighbouring girls' school.
In a 'ghosts of different countries' list, the rival girls' school is placed as Bangladesh's ghost.
Neighbouring girls' schools are compared to snakes based on the colour of their uniforms.
Neighbouring girls' schools lose a competition to our school by a single point and keep explaining excuses.
Roasting the neighbouring girls' school as a mix of scheming and bragging
Students of a rival school try to explain why their school is the best in the district, and their arguments make no sense.
Students of the neighbouring girls' schools are stunned when Annada boys arrive.
why_relatable: Boys'-school students endlessly compare the nearby girls' schools, and group chats turn it into a war
mechanisms_used: 'they hated him because he told the truth' irony

situations: A student accidentally criticises the teacher's favourite political party in front of him and faces his violent wrath.
A teacher hands out transfer certificates (TC) generously to students who bunk or talk in class.
A teacher reacts instantly and violently when a student touches his strongly held personal/religious view
A teacher slaps a laughing student out of nowhere, for no reason at all.
A teacher slaps students for no reason at all, just out of habit.
A teacher suddenly turns and slaps the back-bench student who was chatting during class.
A teacher threatens class 6 kids with a transfer certificate just for making noise, then celebrates the power trip.
A teacher who knows a student hid a mobile phone in the school bag calmly and smugly tells them to take it out.
In a strict teacher's class, one wrong move gets a student beaten with a cane while classmates watch in horror.
why_relatable: Most schools have a teacher with one pet topic where the wrong answer gets you punished on the spot

situations: Caught copying in the exam, a student is moved to the back bench and grieves as if in a sad song.
During JSC/SSC exams, the Brahmanbaria friend sitting behind you keeps cursing at you to show your answers.
During the SSC exam, students of two rival local schools seated together suddenly become allies.
Finding out the strictest teacher is the invigilator in your final exam room kills all hope.
In the exam hall, the student who didn't study gets carried through the exam by copying from friends who studied hard.
In the final exam, students find out the strictest teacher is invigilating their hall, so they sit stiff and act innocent and don't dare to cheat.
One minute before the exam ends, all the answers suddenly start coming back to you.
Students treat the lenient teacher on invigilation duty like a long-awaited messiah.
When the invigilator takes your answer script away at the end of the exam before you have finished, you beg desperately for just a little more time.
why_relatable: Everyone has pleaded for 'one more minute' while the teacher collects scripts with questions still unanswered.

situations: A class teacher fails the whole class out of spite because students take private tuition from a different teacher instead of him.
A student who flopped worst in the monthly coaching test is moved out of the batch with girls as punishment and puts on a brave fake smile.
A teacher who is harsh in school class becomes extremely sweet and friendly in his own paid coaching centre.
Coaching centre ads are so loud and preachy they feel like a politician giving a grand national speech before showing the admission link.
Online/YouTube teachers and coaching-channel lecturers shown as the real heroes who actually taught us
Students argue in the comments over which local coaching centre is the best.
When counting who contributed to a student's education, school classes barely get a hand on the cake while notes, online teachers and self-study take the credit.
why_relatable: Many students learn more from online lecture channels than from school classes

situations: A math teacher solves problems like a kung-fu hero and the girls in his private batch swoon over him, but only in a parallel universe.
A teacher filmed sitting in class on his phone, edited as a hype/fan clip with an over-the-top dialogue.
A teacher in sunglasses dances wildly with students on the tour bus and everyone cheers his name.
A well-known teacher's photo is captioned with his famous catchphrases.
AI-generated cinematic clip showing the school's teachers in a glossy, modern-looking school with a student walking in.
Some students are die-hard fans of one particular teacher and defend him over-the-top
While famous singers brag about being the best, a talented teacher who also sings stays humble and quietly great.
why_relatable: Every school has a teacher with a loyal fan base who take any joke about him personally
mechanisms_used: absurd over-defence ("he's my father, I'm his father")
face-swap of the teacher into the scene

situations: A certain teacher's dialect makes 'take the book' sound like 'take the oar'.
A news headline about Genghis Khan's descendants is used as 'proof' of a teacher's favourite insult.
A teacher who keeps using the same pet insult for students marches into class ready to say it yet again.
A teacher's signature smile is remembered as the warning sign right before trouble begins.
Asked to 'talk dirty', a strict teacher replies with his own trademark classroom phrase.
Misspelling Mangal Shobhajatra as 'Mongol' leads to calling the participants Genghis Khan's descendants, a teacher's favourite insult.
why_relatable: Every school has a teacher with a signature catchphrase that students can predict and imitate.

situations: Students dream of celebrating Eid wildly with friends but have to stay home studying because exams are near.
Two teachers ominously remind students that exams are approaching.
Two teachers solemnly announce that exams are coming, like a doom warning.
When sir announces that anyone who fails the test exam cannot sit for SSC, you react like a fiery protest leader while your friends and the topper look on.
When the teacher announces that anyone who fails the test exam won't be allowed to sit the board exam, the failing students react like fiery protest leaders.
why_relatable: The dread of teachers announcing exams are near is shared by every student.

situations: A fake quote claims a serious teacher will dance to an item song at the school's anniversary celebration.
A spoof entry ID card for the school's alumni festival, edited with laser eyes and a giant beard on a senior alumnus.
Older alumni of the school are shown ending up in very different places, from Saudi Arabia and Canada to Italy via Libya and BUET.
The school's alumni festival welcomes older batches while recent batches are left out and the oldest batches are long gone.
When you go outside your district for higher studies and run into another student from your old school.
why_relatable: Meeting a fellow ex-student far from home creates an instant bond and pride.

situations: A joke mocking the textbook's transgender character 'Sharifa' through a doctor's diagnosis.
A new textbook chapter about gender identity arrives and the whole country panics about it.
Admitting students to the school by lottery instead of an exam is blamed as a devilish idea.
Ordinary people ignore every national problem, but the job quota issue finally wakes them up in fury.
The school founded in 1875 is not called a 150-year tradition, while a procession started in 1985 is called a thousand-year tradition.
why_relatable: Students saw the much-debated new curriculum lesson on 'Sharifa' that sparked national outrage and memes.

situations: A teacher gleefully cooks up a deadly half-yearly exam question paper for class nine.
A teacher puts class 9-10 level questions in the class 7 exam and students stare at the paper in disbelief, then break down.
Students are shocked by a teacher's hard chemistry questions in the exam, then proud when guide and test-paper books print those same questions.
Students relax because an easygoing teacher is setting the question paper, then find a trick question that sounds easy but isn't.
Students' 'sure common' suggestions and 'advance' questions battle each other, but the teacher's own question paper overpowers both.
why_relatable: Everyone has faced a question paper with things never taught in class, set by the one tough teacher.

situations: A nearby small school jumps at every possible occasion to stage dance performances.
Rival schools are told they can only beat Annada in their dreams.
Students of rival local schools present their science fair project with confident nonsense explanations.
The school's founder 'reveals' that a neighbouring rival school is really just part of our school.
why_relatable: Locals know which neighbouring school turns every event into a dance show.

situations: A teacher claims to be politically neutral but his photo posing in a rice paddy field gives away which party he supports.
Teachers assign students a paragraph on the bad effects of smoking and then go smoke themselves.
Teachers give students a paragraph to write on the bad effects of smoking, then go off and smoke themselves.
Teachers stand in the shade looking down at students made to stand in PT under the burning sun.
why_relatable: Students notice the hypocrisy of teachers preaching rules they break themselves.
characters: teachers (Sharif sir, Atik sir, another sir)

situations: A back-bencher squeezes onto the front bench to grab a second tiffin packet.
The class captain inflates the tiffin headcount, and the class teacher inflates that number even further.
The tiffin or treat everyone hoped would be samosas turns out to be plain biscuits.
You buy a tiny cheap plate of chotpoti and six friends each demand 'just one spoon'.
why_relatable: Students suspect everyone up the chain skims extra tiffin packets.

situations: At Eid, ex-students studying at universities all over the country come home and rush back to their old school, climbing the wall like they did when they bunked.
Crying cats in front of the school gate, mourning something about the school.
Four photos show how the school's outer walls and gate have changed, from protest graffiti to election posters to murals to the 150th anniversary gate.
Shots of the school gate, buildings, field and empty classroom are cut against a smiling, dreamy guy remembering the old days.
why_relatable: Ex-students and seniors get hit with nostalgia every time they see the school campus they once wanted to escape.

situations: A local football match at the Tank-er par ground turns into a mass brawl with sticks.
Everyone from Brahmanbaria excitedly shares the news that the local sweet Chhanamukhi got GI status.
The short name of our town, B.Baria, gets rhymed with diarrhea.
The top search suggestion for the hometown is 'simulator', hinting at its reputation for mass fights.
why_relatable: Locals always hear outsiders twist the town's name into embarrassing rhymes.

situations: A teacher looks plain in one photo and stylishly dressed in another, as if he dresses up only for someone special.
A teacher shown first in a plain sports jersey and then in a sharp blazer and sunglasses, as a before/after glow-up.
A teacher's look (party badge, beard, rice sheaf, prayer cap) changes to match whichever political party is in power.
why_relatable: Students notice adults adapting their image to power shifts, a well-known Bangladeshi joke about opportunism.

situations: The class captain has huge attitude, almost no real power, zero respect from classmates, and survives by sucking up to teachers.
You help your friend become class captain, even with fake votes, and he then writes your name on the board as the worst talker.
You rigged votes to make your friend class captain, and he writes your name on the board with three stars for talking.
why_relatable: Class captain elections and the 'names of talkers on the board' ritual are universal, and a friend turning strict after getting power is a classic betrayal.

situations: After getting ragged by seniors at university, ex-students come home and act like cool varsity seniors in front of their school juniors.
Older SSC batches act superior and smug toward newer batches.
Someone messages the page casually as if the admins are juniors, asks their batch, and quickly apologises after learning they are seniors.
why_relatable: Everyone has seen the 'varsity bhai' who shows off at home while keeping quiet about how he's treated on campus.

situations: After standing three hours in the sun for a school event and getting only one patty, the BNCC cadet still brags about the 'special perks' of being a member.
BNCC cadets start acting important and bossy as soon as they put on their uniform, which looks like a guard's dress.
Parody of the viral 'mother favours one child' post, comparing Red Crescent and BNCC members, with BNCC getting the bigger share.
why_relatable: Students in BNCC/scouts do hard duty at every school programme for tiny rewards yet act proud of their privileges.

situations: A parody sob-story where the morning-shift student gets two pieces of meat while the day-shift sibling gets a whole bowl, mocking the status of one shift over the other.
Day-shift students mock morning-shift students who have to wake up at dawn while they are still sleeping.
Someone asks why morning-shift students hang around and eat iftar during day-shift time, and gets beaten up for asking.
why_relatable: Morning and day shift students constantly compete over which shift is better and who gets treated better.

situations: A friend pitches a teacher's private tuition like a motivational speaker selling a life-changing opportunity.
A student who tops a teacher's private tuition batch starts acting superior to everyone else.
A student who writes nonsense in the exam still passes because he studies in the class teacher's private tuition, and others treat him like a god.
why_relatable: Friends always pressure each other to join the same teacher's private batch, hyping it way too much.

situations: A strict chemistry teacher tears apart a student's midterm answer script, crushing hopes of passing.
Once exams end, the teacher happily gets ready to slash marks freely on students' scripts.
When the teacher hands back the half-yearly exam scripts, he turns into a dramatic, ranting performer scolding the whole class.
why_relatable: Class 9 chemistry is a nightmare and the strict teacher's marking makes passing feel impossible.

situations: A friend acts super tough and cool after drinking an energy drink for the first time.
A present-day young man in camouflage uniform roasted with a fake '1971 freedom-fighter archive photo' caption
why_relatable: Friends turn anyone's serious uniform photo (BNCC, scouts, cadet) into a fake-history roast
characters: a classmate or local person ("Dulal" in the caption)

situations: After finishing school, you go back to collect your testimonial and suddenly come face to face with the strict teacher who used to terrorise you, now with nothing to fear.
why_relatable: Ex-students imagine the moment they meet the feared teacher as equals once they've left school.

situations: A teacher feels like a cool boss after scaring noisy students by threatening to give them a TC (transfer certificate).
A teacher who swore a student would fail is stunned and furious when that student gets an A+.
why_relatable: Students love proving wrong the teacher who predicted their failure.

situations: A teacher spends 40 minutes of a 45-minute class giving a motivational speech, and students get bored and fall asleep.
A teacher spends 55 minutes of a one-hour class lecturing that students will later claim there is no studying at school, then looks smugly satisfied.
why_relatable: Every student has sat through a teacher's endless life-lecture instead of the actual lesson.

situations: A student who fears nobody is still terrified of one particular strict teacher.
Three teachers in one photo are matched with a three-headed dragon: two fierce, one goofy.
why_relatable: Students know which teachers are the strict ones and which one is the fun, silly one.

situations: Since people say a spot a teacher beats goes to heaven, the student who gets beaten all the time proudly considers himself guaranteed heaven.
Students joke that a strict teacher's cane is so powerful it would have made enemy soldiers flee.
why_relatable: Students grow up hearing this old saying to justify teacher beatings and joke that they've been beaten enough for full heaven access.

situations: A long-haired, shaggy guy in a clip is compared to a well-known teacher.
A teacher's heavily edited flowery profile photos look like the groom shots from old wedding videos.
why_relatable: Students stalk teachers' Facebook pictures and love laughing at their over-edited, old-fashioned photos.

situations: After a strict teacher is promoted and transferred to another school, TCs issued there skyrocket.
When a teacher leaves or is transferred, students react with exaggerated (possibly fake or happy) tears.
why_relatable: At every teacher's farewell students act heartbroken, even when they are secretly relieved.

situations: When a teacher cracks an unfunny joke in class, the first-bench nerds laugh hysterically to please him.
why_relatable: Every class has front-benchers who over-laugh at the teacher's weak jokes to stay in his good books, while the rest of the class cringes.

situations: The class finally catches the classmate who used to spy and snitch to the teacher, and everyone piles on him.
why_relatable: Every class has an informer who reports talkers and bunkers to sir, and everyone secretly dreams of revenge.

situations: Rival guidebook and suggestion brands fight for students before exams, with one beating another while a third looks on.
why_relatable: Every student knows the guide-book brands and has argued about which one's suggestions 'came common' in the exam.
characters: guide-book brands (Sure Common, Advance, Popy Guide)

situations: An old colonial-era record shows the school existed in 1875 and already had a library of 3903 books.
why_relatable: Students love proof that their school is old and historic.

situations: When the teacher asks who wrote on the bench, everyone looks around innocently as if they know nothing.
why_relatable: Bench graffiti is everywhere, and nobody ever admits to it.

situations: The whole class scrambles back to their seats the moment word spreads that a strict teacher is coming.
why_relatable: Every class has one teacher whose arrival turns chaos into instant silence and panic.

situations: A friend hypes up a fun outing, but when you get there the place is full of your own teachers and you feel trapped.
why_relatable: Every student has been dragged to an 'enjoyable' event (rally, fair, programme) only to find strict teachers there, killing the fun.
characters: teachers (real photo, one grinning, one grumpy)

situations: After a teacher complains about a student at the parents' meeting, his mother comes home and knocks on his door holding something to beat him with.
why_relatable: Every student fears the parents' meeting where a teacher reports their behaviour and the beating that follows at home.

situations: A teacher promises the exact exam questions, but his 'suggestion' turns out to be every board question of chapter 1, all of chapter 2 and the whole book.
why_relatable: Students beg for a short suggestion before exams and teachers (especially private tutors) give a 'suggestion' that covers the entire syllabus.

situations: A student asks the teacher whether he'll get marks in the exam, and the teacher replies 'you'll get a number — zero'.
why_relatable: Students anxiously ask teachers about marks and get savage, witty answers that crush their hope.

situations: Someone keeps getting mistaken for a famous film actor and is tired of explaining he's not him.
why_relatable: Students love saying a teacher or classmate looks like a celebrity and won't let it go.

situations: Boys claim they are just waiting for the school's national-day rally, but they are really there to watch girls pass by.
why_relatable: Rallies and day-observance programs are known excuses to see students from girls' schools.

situations: Two teachers are fighting; the page pretends to separate them, then hands them boxing gloves and enjoys the show.
why_relatable: Students love the drama when teachers clash and secretly fan the flames.

situations: The moment the teacher steps out of class for two minutes, the whole class erupts into a party.
why_relatable: Every class turns into chaos the second the teacher leaves the room.

situations: After someone lets out a terrible fart in class, the backbenchers celebrate as if they won a trophy.
why_relatable: Backbenchers turn every embarrassing class moment into a celebration.

situations: Late students locked out at the school gate react like angry protesters giving fiery speeches.
why_relatable: Arriving late and finding the gate shut is a daily drama every student has faced or witnessed.

situations: Instead of copying notes from the board, a student takes a photo, promising to write it at home (and never does).
why_relatable: Everyone has photographed the board with full intention to copy later and then forgotten about it.

situations: Sitting in the hall room during a boring class, a portrait on the wall seems to stare straight at you as if it knows what you did.
why_relatable: Students know the old portraits in the hall room and the feeling of being watched while misbehaving.

situations: A teacher solves a math problem wrongly on the board and angrily refuses to accept it when a student points out the mistake.
why_relatable: Students have all seen a teacher get defensive instead of admitting an error, which makes correcting them risky.

situations: A teacher sees a student's meme, smiles, and asks who his class teacher is, meaning trouble is coming.
why_relatable: Students fear their teachers finding the meme page and tracing the jokes back to them.

situations: The school wall has a 'No writing or posters' sign, but it ends up completely covered in political posters anyway.
why_relatable: Students walk past their school wall every day and see official rules being openly ignored, especially during election season.

situations: After arguing with the class bully during class, a student runs into him outside school at the local pond bank and suddenly turns very polite and apologetic.
why_relatable: Everyone acts brave inside the classroom, then gets scared when they meet the class tough guy outside, where no teacher can protect them.
